newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu "steaming" over tales about his wife.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu "steaming" over tales about his wife.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu fumed on Monday over more unflattering publicity about the wife he thrust into the public eye.
"If you ask me if I'm angry -- very much so. If you ask me if I'm steaming -- I'm steaming. It has to stop now," Netanyahu told Army Radio.

The latest furore erupted after a new book about Netanyahu's ascent to power detailed what it said was a fiery phone conversation last year between the first lady and Communications Minister Limor Livnat.
Sara Netanyahu refused Livnat's request to speak to the prime minister, according to excerpts of the book carried by an Israeli television station and a newspaper.

"It's Friday night. I ask you not to call at these hours. Bibi is with the children. You phone here all the time and it is very disturbing," Mrs Netanyahu replied before the conversation became a shouting match punctuated by curses, the book said.
In Israel, where a politician's wife has traditionally stayed in her husband's shadow, such behaviour strains the boundary between protection of privacy and intervention in state affairs.
Asked if Sara, his third wife, intervened in his political life, Netanyahu told the radio: "Not at all. It is all nonsense. They took a minor event and blew it out of all proportion."

The Likud leader, running a U.S.-style campaign, put Sara in the media spotlight in last year's election. Embracing the wife he had admitted cheating on, Netanyahu sought to show he had put his own house in order before tackling Israel's problems.
Since taking office, Mrs Netanyahu has figured in unflattering reports about her alleged domineering behaviour towards underlings ranging from her children's nannies to her husband's aides.

The former flight attendant has also stirred controversy by accompanying her husband on almost all his official trips abroad and sometimes taking the kids. Former Prime Minister Shimon Peres's wife usually stayed grounded.
